data.name: InvalidArray
data.value: Enter 4–80 integers from 1 to 10000, separated by commas or whitespace.

data.name: ComplexityNote
data.value: Counts the comparisons/reads and swaps/writes recorded by the simulator; not runtime or all CPU operations. Reference curves are scaled at the largest n, not proof of Big-O.

data.name: CompareNote
data.value: Both algorithms use identical input. Each tick advances one recorded step; step count is not CPU time. A finished side keeps its result.

data.name: GraphHelp
data.value: Undirected graph. Each line: source, destination, weight. Nodes start at 0. BFS/DFS ignore weights; Dijkstra requires nonnegative weights; Prim finds the minimum spanning tree of the start component.

data.name: InvalidGraph
data.value: Use 2–12 nodes, a valid start, and at most 40 edges. Each line needs three integers: u v w; no self-loops or duplicate edges, weights 0–99.

data.name: FibonacciHelp
data.value: F(0)=0, F(1)=1; F(i)=F(i−1)+F(i−2). Each step fills one cell from the previous two.

data.name: KnapsackHelp
data.value: 0/1 knapsack: use each item at most once. dp[i,c] is the best value using the first i items and capacity c. Choose the larger of skipping or taking the item if it fits.

data.name: LcsHelp
data.value: Longest common subsequence: equal characters → diagonal + 1; otherwise → max(above, left). A subsequence need not be contiguous.

data.name: InvalidDP
data.value: Fibonacci: n from 0–30. Knapsack: 1–8 items, weights 1–20, values 1–10000, capacity 1–20. LCS: up to 12 characters per string.

data.name: BubbleQuestion
data.value: What is the worst-case time complexity of Bubble Sort?

data.name: BubbleExplanation
data.value: A reversed array needs repeated passes of comparisons and swaps, growing quadratically.

data.name: BinaryQuestion
data.value: What is worst-case search time in a BST that degenerates into a chain?

data.name: BinaryExplanation
data.value: The height can be n−1; search may visit every node.

data.name: StableQuestion
data.value: What does a stable sort preserve?

data.name: StableExplanation
data.value: Records with equal keys retain their original relative order.

data.name: BfsQuestion
data.value: Which structure does BFS use to visit level by level?

data.name: BfsExplanation
data.value: FIFO processes earlier discoveries first, giving shortest paths by edge count in an unweighted graph.

data.name: DijkstraQuestion
data.value: Which edge-weight condition guarantees Dijkstra correctness?

data.name: DijkstraExplanation
data.value: A negative edge can improve a settled node, breaking the greedy assumption.

data.name: PrimQuestion
data.value: What does Prim find in a connected undirected graph?

data.name: PrimExplanation
data.value: Prim chooses the lightest edge connecting the current tree to a node outside it.

data.name: KnapsackQuestion
data.value: In 0/1 knapsack, how many times can each item be selected?

data.name: KnapsackExplanation
data.value: Taking item i uses the previous row i−1, preventing reuse of that item.

data.name: LcsOption2
data.value: Longest common subsequence, not necessarily contiguous

data.name: LcsExplanation
data.value: For example, AC is a common subsequence of ABC and ADC even though its characters are not adjacent.

data.name: GraphMetrics
data.value: BFS shows minimum edge counts; DFS shows traversal-tree depth, not shortest paths. Dijkstra shows total path weights; Prim shows the edge weight connecting each node to the tree.
